text.p: Manufacturing and investment firm Austrim Ltd said on Monday that it planned to raise A$208 million from a two-for-five renounceable rights issue to reduce debt and for working capital purposes.
It said the rights would be offered to shareholders at A$3.30 each.
Austrim, which is led by former BTR Plc boss Alan Jackson, has been on the acquisition trail for the past year.
Most recently, it reached an agreement to buy auto parts and engineering group Hawker Richardson Ltd and now has about 40 percent of the company. The bid values Hawker at about A$68 million.
Earlier in the year, Austrim bought a South Australian vehicle hire and workshop business for A$41 million and the Calum textiles operation for A$53 million.
Austrim shares were five cents higher at A$3.85 at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), 10 cents off its 1997 high.
Austrim said the prospectus for the rights issue was expected to be mailed to shareholders on August 18.
